scope: Author-led comparison of every executable library model with its primary publication at the stated evidence level. The historical _ddi suffix is ignored for scientific scope. This is not an independent reproduction of the source analysis.

resultDefinitions.ARTICLE_ALIGNED: Published structure, fixed effects, covariates, variability and residual model are represented without an identified structural adaptation.
resultDefinitions.DOCUMENTED_ADAPTATION_CONFIRMED: The executable model differs from the publication, and every identified difference is explicitly documented in model code and catalog metadata.
resultDefinitions.SOURCE_AMBIGUITY_DOCUMENTED: The publication contains an ambiguity that cannot be resolved without the source control stream or supplementary model files. The retained interpretation is explicit.

evidenceDefinitions.LOCAL_PRIMARY_FULL_TEXT: Primary article PDF reviewed locally; the private PDF is excluded from Git.
evidenceDefinitions.OPEN_PRIMARY_FULL_TEXT: Primary full text reviewed from an open publisher or repository copy.
evidenceDefinitions.PRIMARY_ABSTRACT_ONLY: Primary abstract and bibliographic record reviewed; equation-level verification remains limited.
evidenceDefinitions.PRIMARY_ABSTRACT_PLUS_SECONDARY_FULL_TEX: Primary abstract reviewed and parameter context cross-checked against a full secondary scientific source.

reviewed.note: The executable file represents the base model from Table 2, not the final covariate model. It remains simulation-only.
Published CL/F, Q/F, V1/F, V2/F and reported IIV replace the previous mismatched values. Absorption and residual terms remain explicit simulation assumptions pending the full model specification.
Two-compartment structure, creatinine-clearance effect, variability and proportional residual error align with the article. The zero additive variance only satisfies the two-term engine contract.

Published fixed effects and the renal and weight relationships are retained. The printed clearance relationship requires an explicit centered implementation choice, and only CL IIV is represented; simulation only.
Fixed and random-effect values align with Table 2; the oral transit chain remains a reconstruction because executable transit equations are absent from the main article.
The source NPAG model is nonparametric; the log-normal OMEGA prior is an explicit mapbayr approximation.
The final unbound-concentration equations, including the published Q exponent 0.78, are retained. Published occasion variability is omitted.
Two-compartment structure, CKD-EPI effect, correlated CL-Vc block, Q/Vp variability and proportional residual error now use the published Monolix omega scale.
Published CL and V1 inter-occasion effects are omitted and the combined1 residual SD is represented by the engine's combined2 error. The model remains simulation-only.
Renal, CRRT and nonrenal clearance components, volumes, IIV and combined residual error align with the final model; NONMEM omega percentages are encoded as squared SDs.
Structure, dialysis branch, fixed effects and random-effect scale align with the publication.
Structure, Cockcroft-Gault effect, fixed effects, IIV and proportional residual error align with Table 2; NONMEM omega percentages are encoded as squared SDs.

Published weight scaling, prednisolone effects, IIV and residual model are retained and the unsupported CYP3A5 baseline effect was removed. IOV on F is omitted; the CYP3A fraction is an interaction-only adaptation.
The source is a nonlinear dose-ranging NCA study, not a PopPK model. The module is now explicitly limited to the published 50 mg steady-state CL/F and Vz/F; ka and random effects are assumptions.
The two-compartment equations, dialysis, sex and infection effects and LC-MS/MS residual error align with the publication.
Published fixed effects and between-subject variability are retained; inter-occasion variability on CL and V1 is omitted.

The source reports biphasic IV disposition and summary NCA values rather than a reusable PopPK model. The executable profile now uses the published 70 kg mean CL, V and F in a documented one-compartment approximation; ka is assumed.

The source reports formulation-, meal- and occasion-dependent bioavailability after individual IV characterization, not a reusable PopPK model. F=0.40 represents base after meals; CL, V and ka are declared assumptions.
Published fixed effects and reported IIV are retained. The TDM-induced dose-clearance association is deliberately omitted, pragmatic Q/V2 variances are added and the CYP3A split is interaction-only.
The mechanistic structure and published parameters are retained. Liver volume is approximated, MAT IOV is represented as IIV and the non-CYP fraction is interaction-only.
The cited source is a clinical PK review, not a PopPK model. Published mean CL, F and half-life-derived V are used; ka and random effects are documented simulation assumptions.
The publication is ambiguous about lean versus total body weight for V; the engine's total-weight choice is documented.
The article does not provide the exact corrected lean-body-mass and Cockcroft-Gault variants; the implemented choices are documented.
Cockcroft-Gault substitution, albumin bounds and unreported Q/V2 allometric assumptions are documented engine adaptations.
Clinical formulas are reconstructed from available covariates; unreported covariance and V1 variability are not invented.
Clinical formulas are reconstructed from available covariates; unreported covariance and V1 variability are not invented.
Weibull absorption, race and patient-status effects, BMI effect and reported IIV are retained. Patient CL variability and one residual branch are used by default instead of study-specific branches.
The cited work is an NCA DDI study and provides no reusable PopPK model. The entry is explicitly a rounded mean-profile reconstruction for interaction simulation, not an article model or MAP prior.
One-compartment oral structure, renal and age covariates, variability and residual error align with the article.
The irreversible bone compartment is omitted for repeated-dose plasma simulation, and unpublished residual terms are marked pragmatic.
The publication reports an individual PK analysis; its use as a population prior is an explicit simulation-only adaptation.
Oral bioavailability and the female Cockcroft-Gault factor are engine assumptions; the published platelet PD component is out of scope.

The previous mismatched CL, V, ka and F were replaced by the published one-compartment lag model and its medication and clinical covariates. Patient-study IIV/error are defaults instead of separate study branches.
The printed BMI effect on CL lacks an operator before 6.22; the retained historical interpretation is explicitly flagged.
Published transit absorption and time-dependent autoinduction are retained. HIV, nutritional supplementation, continuation-phase, between-occasion effects and most random effects are omitted.
One-compartment oral structure and reported fixed, random and residual parameters align with the article.
Published chronic-dose CL and F replace the previous mismatched clearance. V and ka are not reported in the accessible source summary and remain explicit mean-profile assumptions.
The final additive estimate 2.256 mg/L is implemented as an SD and squared for mrgsolve. The article also mentions log-transformed data despite its concentration-scale equation.

Published typical values, lag, lopinavir effect and IIV replace the previous generic module. IOV on F, V-ka covariance and the two-population residual mixture are omitted; the dominant residual component is used.
Published two-compartment Erlang structure, fixed effects and additive CYP3A5 clearance effect are retained. Several variances and the interaction-only non-CYP fraction are pragmatic.

Published fixed effects, weight allometry, correlated CL-V1 block, KTR variability and lag class replace the prior Woillard-derived variability and unsupported CYP effect. CL IOV and per-sample residual switching are omitted; DDI splitting is interaction-only.
Published Prograf/Advagraf PK, covariates, IIV and residual model are retained. The interaction clearance split preserves baseline clearance exactly and is the only non-source mechanism.

Primary-article Methods and Table 2 were re-reviewed locally. The implementation now uses the published serum-creatinine floor of 1 mg/dL when age is >60 years, caps calculated Cockcroft-Gault CrCl at 150 mL/min, and retains the published CL/V1/Q/V2, dialysis, IIV and residual-error values. Independent synthetic source-equation and MAP-oracle tests include both renal boundaries. This is not external validation; DIAL remains a static study-status covariate.
The Revilla equations, measured 24-hour creatinine clearance and additive residual SD align with the article.
The continuous-infusion structure, measured 24-hour creatinine clearance and published parameter values align with the article.
Published nonlinear one-compartment structure, CRP effect and fixed parameters are retained. Only Vmax IIV is represented and the residual prior is an engine adaptation; simulation only.
